newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow critical of planned Chechnya cabinet - agency.
newsitem.headline: Moscow critical of planned Chechnya cabinet - agency.

text.p: A senior Russian official said on Sunday that Moscow would not recognise the Chechen government currently drafted by separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, Interfax news agency reported.
It quoted a "senior government source" as saying that the decision was made on Saturday at a meeting of top officials chaired by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
But Moscow security tsar Alexander Lebed, who had struck a peace deal with Chechen separatists on August 31, said in a conflicting statement that he was unaware of any such decision.
"What we were talking about is adjusting the peace process in Chechnya," Ekho Moskvy quoted Lebed, who attended Saturday's meeting, as saying.
President Boris Yeltsin who normally chairs such top-level meetings is currently preparing for heart surgery.

The agreement struck by Lebed and rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov provided for a Russian troop withdrawal in exchange for a five-year deferral on the decision on Chechnya's future political status, the most sensitive issue behind the conflict.
The deal also included the creation of a joint commission to run the region after the planned Russian troop withdrawal and until the next Chechen elections.
Lebed insists that other top officials had no formal objections to the deal that stopped the 21-month war.
But his claim of unconditional backing from Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin and other Russian leaders have been repeatedly played down by their press offices.
The Kremlin leaders have said they saw preserving Russia's territorial integrity as a priority task of any peace deal.

The rebels, who say they still stick to their plans of winning full independence, saw the peace deal as their victory and started replacing Moscow-installed administrations throughout Chechnya with their own.
Yandarbiyev has said he was ready to offer up to 14 seats in his cabinet to other Chechen groups and even to invite members of the pro-Moscow government of Doku Zavgayev.
Zavgayev has said he would not cooperate with rebels on such terms and has branded his former aides who agreed to join Yandarbiyev's government as "renegades".
Interfax quoted the government source as saying that Moscow would deal only with the still non-existent joint commission which he said should include all major Chechen forces.
"The commission should consist of two equal teams: the federal delegation and representatives of the Chechen republic," the source said.
"Supporters of Yandarbiyev, Zavgayev as well as representatives of other parties and movements should have certain quotas in the second team," he added.

The source said that Russia was ready to offer funds for the reconstruction of Chechnya only to the joint commission. The deal signed by Lebed and Yandarbiyev did not contain any details of the joint commission.
